guidance: Planning estimate, not a production budget. The page count assumes the pasted text keeps the script's own line breaks and the 55-line page; a reflowed PDF, a proportional font or dropped page breaks all count differently, so check the eighths against the actual script pages.
method: A formatted screenplay page is a fixed grid rather than a fixed amount of prose: 12-point Courier, 1-inch top and bottom margins and about 55 lines to the page regardless of paper size, which is why crews measure a script in pages and eighths of a page. The page counts the lines of the pasted text after normalising CRLF, CR and form feeds to line breaks and dropping blank lines at the very start and end, divides by the lines per page entered (30 to 70), and rounds up to the next whole eighth, so 55 lines at 55 a page is one page, 56 lines is 1 1/8 pages and a partial eighth is never dropped. A scene heading is a line that starts, after an optional scene number such as 12A, with INT, EXT, INT./EXT, EXT./INT or I/E, a dot being optional and the match case-insensitive; the prefix sets interior, exterior or mixed. The time of day is the text after the last spaced hyphen, en dash or em dash of the heading, with any parenthetical removed and a trailing full stop dropped: exactly DAY counts as day, exactly NIGHT as night, and DAWN, DUSK, CONTINUOUS, LATER, MAGIC HOUR or anything else counts as other. A heading with no spaced separator, or with nothing after it, is reported as having no time of day, and the line it sits on is listed. Scene numbers are uppercase and may carry a letter; a number used more than once is reported once, however many times it repeats, and unnumbered headings are counted separately. The estimate assumes the paste keeps the script's own line breaks: a PDF copy that reflows paragraphs, a draft in a proportional font or a file whose page breaks were dropped all count differently, blank lines inside the text count towards the page because they hold a line position, and the page count says nothing about running time. A script longer than 2,000,000 characters is refused so that one act is pasted at a time.

sources.title: Nashville Film Institute, Screenplay Format: Everything You Need to Know - the standard on-page style, about 55 lines per page excluding the page number, and the INT./EXT. location plus time-of-day scene heading
